labels.name: Disease
labels.description: A disease, syndrome, or pathological pattern in Traditional Chinese Medicine or biomedicine (e.g. common cold, exterior wind-cold, qi deficiency).

properties.name: name
properties.description: Canonical display name of the disease or pattern.

labels.name: Effect
labels.description: A therapeutic action or function claimed for a herb or formula (e.g. tonify qi, induce sweating, clear heat).

properties.name: name
properties.description: Canonical display name of the therapeutic effect.

labels.name: Formula
labels.description: A multi-herb prescription / decoction used in Traditional Chinese Medicine (e.g. Ephedra Decoction / Ma Huang Tang).

properties.name: classification
properties.description: Formula category in TCM formulary taxonomy (e.g. exterior-releasing, tonifying).

properties.name: contraindications
properties.description: Conditions, patient types, or situations in which the formula should not be used.

properties.name: dosage
properties.description: Administration and dosage instructions for the formula.

properties.name: key_diagnostic_points
properties.description: Key clinical signs and diagnostic criteria that indicate use of the formula.

properties.name: name
properties.description: Canonical display name of the formula, usually English with Pinyin in parentheses.

labels.name: Herb
labels.description: A medicinal herb or materia medica item used alone or as a formula ingredient (e.g. Ephedra / Ma Huang).

properties.name: contraindications
properties.description: Conditions or patient types for which the herb is contraindicated or should be used with caution.

properties.name: dosage
properties.description: Typical dosage and usage instructions for the herb.

properties.name: flavor
properties.description: Taste / flavor property in TCM (e.g. bitter, sweet, acrid).

properties.name: meridians
properties.description: Channels / meridians the herb enters (list of meridian names).

properties.name: name
properties.description: Canonical display name of the herb, usually English with Pinyin in parentheses.

properties.name: nature
properties.description: Temperature / nature property in TCM (e.g. hot, warm, neutral, cool, cold).

properties.name: preparation_method
properties.description: Cultivation, processing, or preparation method of the medicinal material.

properties.name: scientific_name
properties.description: Latin / botanical scientific name of the plant or material.

labels.name: Source
labels.description: A classical or modern textual source that cites a herb or formula (e.g. Treatise on Cold Damage / Shang Han Lun).

properties.name: name
properties.description: Canonical display name of the textual source.

labels.name: Symptom
labels.description: A clinical symptom or sign (e.g. fever, aversion to cold, wheezing, headache).

properties.name: name
properties.description: Canonical display name of the symptom or sign.

relationships.description: A Formula or Herb is indicated for treating a Disease or pattern.
A Disease (or pattern) presents with a Symptom, or is clinically associated with another Disease-level presentation.
A Formula or Herb relieves or improves a Symptom (or a disease-like presentation labeled as such in the source text).
A Formula or Herb possesses a therapeutic Effect / function.
A Formula or Herb is recorded in or cited from a textual Source.
A Formula (or compound preparation) contains a Herb ingredient, or nests another Formula as a component.

triples.description: A disease or pattern presents with a given clinical symptom.
A disease or pattern is associated with another disease-level presentation (e.g. nested or overlapping patterns in the source text).
A formula is recorded in or attributed to a classical or modern textual source.
A formula contains a medicinal herb as an ingredient.
A formula is indicated for treating a disease or pattern.
A formula relieves or improves a clinical symptom.
A formula has a stated therapeutic effect or function.
A formula incorporates another formula as a component (nested prescription).
A formula is indicated against a symptom-like presentation that was typed as a treatment target in the source extraction.
A herb is indicated for treating a disease or pattern.
A herb has a stated therapeutic effect or function.
A herb relieves or improves a clinical symptom.
A herb is recorded in or attributed to a classical or modern textual source.
A herb is described as relieving a disease-level presentation that appears under an alleviation relation in the source text.
A herb is indicated against a symptom-like presentation typed as a treatment target in the source extraction.
A herb preparation includes another herb as a component (e.g. processed product or pair).
A symptom is linked to a disease or pattern it commonly accompanies (direction as stored in the graph).
